heuristic.applicability: Prefer close_drawer__h04 at an early placement-to-closure handoff when drawer_position is near the open value, the measured TCP is close to the observed block, object_pose is considered reliable, and the block/TCP pair may be translated relative to its demonstrated location. It remains callable at later valid phases because its gate becomes zero and the action frame is then exactly target_pose. Prefer h01 for coherent displacement of the whole drawer assembly, h02 when local realized-TCP mismatch dominates, and h03 when already-partial closure or stopping ambiguity dominates.

handoff.entry_conditions: The drawer is open near 0.300 m. At the earliest shared entry the block may still be descending/releasing near the TCP or may already rest inside the cavity; later valid entries may be during retreat, handle approach, or closure. For the targeted block-anchor behavior, require a reliable object_pose and an early state with the TCP close to the block. Do not treat the gate as proof of grasp or safe placement.
handoff.exit_conditions: Use the unchanged terminal guidance: drawer_position below 0.025 m with negligible velocity, block retained inside near the drawer floor, fingers open, and TCP retreated high and clear. Framework task success is unchanged.
handoff.failure_signatures: An incorrect active block gate can make the TCP chase or re-contact a noisy/moving block, fail to clear the cavity, or bias handle approach. If an early displaced block is already farther than 0.16 m from the TCP, the gate is zero and the targeted invariance is absent. Other failures are missed handle acquisition, drawer stopping above 0.025 m, block leaving/interfering with the drawer, jam, collision, or unconverged/unreachable IK.
handoff.overlap_role: All actions 900:1160 remain directly diffusion-supervised in all 12 trajectories: 260 actions (13.0 s) per trajectory shared with place_block_in_drawer. This covers release completion under different observed block heights/finger openings, initial clearance, retreat/reorientation, handle approach and acquisition before active closure.
handoff.successor_readiness: This is terminal. Readiness is observable only from the unchanged physical criteria: loaded drawer closed below 0.025 m and nearly stationary, gripper released, and hand clear. The learned phase and analytic gate are not success predicates.

heuristic.limitations: The smooth gate is a geometric phase prior, not contact detection. It assumes valid placement keeps the block away from the later handle corridor and that target_pose remains a coherent drawer-attached frame. It can be wrong under noisy/occluded object_pose, a fast or bouncing block, a block displaced toward the handle, or an unusual early state with large TCP-block separation. Translation covariance does not remove fixed-base reachability, joint-limit, collision, handle-geometry, force/contact, or orientation dependencies. No recovery from missed release, missed grasp, jam, obstruction, collision, or unreachable targets is demonstrated, and no out-of-distribution benefit is observed.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Add h04 as an independent selectable terminal close-drawer policy, not a replacement selected from the in-distribution scores. A high-level agent can prefer it using observable geometry when the open drawer and close TCP-block relation indicate unfinished release and block displacement is the concern. The receiver must preserve both causal history frames across the switch. Continue invoking until the unchanged physical exit rule is satisfied; if the block pose is unreliable or the gate conditions conflict with scene semantics, select an existing prior rather than relying on h04.
heuristic.rationale: The three immutable policies each passed all 12 in-distribution replay-entry validations, so there is no observed in-distribution deficit to repair. The demonstrations nevertheless expose a difficult early handoff: at index 900, object z spans about 0.063-0.124 m and finger width spans about 0.0365-0.0765 m before the common retreat and handle sequence. H04 targets an untested spatial variant of that handoff: translation of the block/TCP release interaction relative to the drawer target. For each causal state define g_open=clip((drawer_position-0.24)/0.04,0,1), g_near=clip((0.16-||p_tcp-p_object||)/0.08,0,1), and g=g_open*g_near. The anchor has target_pose orientation and translation p_target+g*(p_object-p_target). Thus it equals the observed block translation when the fully open drawer and close TCP-block relation indicate release, blends smoothly during clearance, and equals target_pose for handle approach/closure. Labels and decoded commands are full TCP poses relative to this freshly recomputed anchor. The intended benefit is block-translation covariance for release completion and initial clearance without letting normal settled-block variation translate the handle trajectory. Target-relative observations retain drawer geometry, while qpos/qvel and fingers retain reachability, posture and gripper dependencies. This benefit is falsifiable but unconfirmed because no OOD validation exists.
heuristic.statement: Adaptive interaction-anchor Cartesian Diffusion Policy: express each commanded TCP pose in a smooth causal frame that follows observed block translation only during the open-drawer, TCP-near-block release neighborhood and otherwise is the drawer-attached target_pose. This makes release completion and initial clearance covariant to block displacement by construction while preserving drawer-relative handle approach, closure, release and retreat.

assignment.subgoal: Ensure the block is released inside the open drawer, retreat from the cavity, approach and grasp the drawer handle, push the drawer from about 0.30 m travel to below the 0.025 closed threshold, release the handle, and retreat to a clear final pose. The intended contact target after release is the drawer handle; at early overlap states the block may still be the object being lowered/released and must not be confused with the handle. Approximate exit: drawer_position about 0.0022, block enclosed at z=0.063, open fingers, TCP high and clear.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: Using the same pre-action observation for the deterministic anchor, compare FK of decoded IK joints with the demonstrated commanded TCP target in metres/radians and compare the unchanged gripper scalar. Rotation 6D is deterministically projected to SO(3); unconverged IK is returned with explicit diagnostics rather than replaced.

contract.cut_relation: Uses every assigned action in [900,1330) for all 12 trajectories. The complete [900,1160) action-supervised overlap with place_block_in_drawer is preserved; only causal coordinates and the Cartesian action reference frame are changed.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is [adaptive-anchor xyz metres, adaptive-anchor relative rotation 6D, native gripper scalar]. The anchor orientation is target_pose orientation. Its world translation is p_target + g*(p_object-p_target), where g=clip((drawer_position-0.24)/0.04,0,1)*clip((0.16-||p_tcp-p_object||)/0.08,0,1). Labels use the corresponding slot's pre-action observation; decoding recomputes the anchor from the fresh current observation. The 6D pair is projected by Gram-Schmidt to SO(3), composed with the anchor to a world TCP target, and passed to panda_kinematics.solve_ik from fresh measured joints. Gripper >=0 opens and <0 closes. Slots represent t-1 through t+14; execution uses slots 1 through 8 beginning at current t.
contract.parameter_semantics: No high-level arguments. target_pose and object_pose are observed world poses in metres with wxyz quaternions, and drawer_position is metres. The executor supplies two causal observations and a fresh observation for each decoded slot. The adaptive interaction anchor is recomputed from those observations identically in training and deployment.
